citation: Olson, C. B., Matuchniak, T., Chung, H. Q., Stumpf, R., & Farkas, G. (2017). Reducing achievement gaps in academic writing for Latinos and English learners in Grades 7-12. Journal of Educational Psychology, 109(1), 1-21. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000095
report_number: Journal of Educational Psychology 109(1):1-21 (DOI 10.1037/edu0000095). Funded by U.S. Department of Education, Office of English Language Acquisition (Pathway to Academic Success Project). Extracted from the APA-hosted author accepted-manuscript (publisher CHORUS public-access copy at psycnet.apa.org/manuscript/2016-21264-001.pdf).
design: Multi-site cluster-randomized controlled trial (assignment = teacher/class within school). Anaheim Union High School District (AUHSD), CA -- a large, urban, low-SES district (98% Latino, 88% mainstreamed English learners). This is a NEW district replication of the earlier Santa Ana (SAUSD) Pathway RCT (Olson et al. 2012, row 86); distinct from the four-district scale-up (Olson et al. 2020, row 88). 95 teachers in 16 secondary schools (8 middle, 8 high) were stratified by grade within school and randomly assigned to Pathway (49) vs business-as-usual control (46); one focal class per teacher was randomly selected; students were randomly assigned to teachers' classes. Intervention = Pathway Project teacher PD, 46 hours/year of training (six 6-hour released days + five 2-hour afterschool sessions) plus coaching, teaching a cognitive-strategies approach to text-based analytical reading/writing; comparison = business-as-usual district training. Grades 7-12. Two implementation years analyzed as separate student cohorts: Year 1 = 2012-2013 (analysis sample 93 teachers, 47 Pathway + 46 control classrooms, N=1817 students); Year 2 = 2013-2014 (analysis sample 81 teachers, 41 Pathway + 40 control classrooms, N=1250 students; Year-2 students are first-year-program students taught by second-year-program teachers). Impacts on the Academic Writing Assessment (AWA, on-demand analytical essay scored 2-12) estimated by gain-score regression (post minus pre regressed on Pathway dummy + demographic controls) with standard errors corrected for clustering of students within teachers' classes via the Huber-White sandwich estimator (STATA cluster command); Cohen's d = Pathway coefficient / pooled pretest SD. CAHSEE (California High School Exit Exam) 10th-grade pass rates analyzed by cluster-robust logistic regression.
problems: SOURCE (legal OA): the version of record is the APA Journal of Educational Psychology article (DOI 10.1037/edu0000095). OpenAlex/Unpaywall flag it as hybrid 'other-oa' but APA serves the publisher landing page behind a 403/paywall with no direct OA PDF. I did NOT use any pirated copy. I extracted from the APA-hosted author accepted manuscript released through APA's CHORUS public-access program (the same 73-page PDF whose cover page reads 'Manuscript version of ... (c) 2016 American Psychological Association ... The final version of record is available via its DOI'), downloaded directly from psycnet.apa.org -- a legitimate publisher/funder public-access source, permitted by the spec. The accepted manuscript is content-identical to the published article for all reported statistics (abstract Year 1 d=0.48, Year 2 d=0.60 match the published figures). KEY POINTS / AMBIGUITIES: (1) The headline outcome is the Academic Writing Assessment (AWA), a RESEARCHER/DEVELOPER-MADE on-demand analytical-essay measure scored 2-12 -- writing -> outcome_subject Other. The meta-analysis (Visscher et al.) restricted to INDEPENDENT measures, so the AWA likely did NOT enter the meta-analysis pool; the only independent/standardized achievement outcome here is the CAHSEE (a state high-school exit exam). I extract both and label test_type, per spec ('extract whatever achievement outcomes are reported and label the type -- we filter centrally'). (2) Years 1 and 2 are SEPARATE student cohorts (different students each year), so both are valid distinct post-intervention contrasts on different samples rather than repeated waves of one cohort; I extract both and mark Year 2 as the end-of-treatment/headline replication. (3) AWA impacts are the covariate/pretest-adjusted gain-score regression coefficients (Table 6 Model 2 for Year 1: b=0.96, SE=0.20; Model B for Year 2: b=1.30, SE=0.20), standardized by the pooled pretest SD (Year 1 SD~2.00 giving d=0.48; Year 2 SD~2.167 giving d=0.60), exactly reproducing the paper's reported d. SEs are cluster-robust (Huber-White by classroom) so cluster_adjusted=true. (4) CAHSEE is a DICHOTOMOUS pass/fail outcome on 10th-graders ONLY (a non-randomised grade subset of the full 7-12 sample), so is_full_sample=false and outcome_role=secondary for those rows; g is derived from the odds ratio via the Cox/logit transform (d=ln(OR)/1.65) -- an approximation, flagged. For CAHSEE I record the UNADJUSTED pass-rate contrast (Table 7/8, statistically significant) in mean_t/mean_c and impact_estimate, because the covariate-adjusted logistic models (Table 9) became non-significant due to small 10th-grade subsamples and the authors explicitly call the CAHSEE regression results 'suggestive rather than definitive'; the adjusted OR-based g is given in notes. (5) ICC not reported (NOT guessed; icc=null); n_clusters = number of teachers/classrooms in each year's AWA analysis sample (Year1=93, Year2=81) or in the CAHSEE 10th-grade subsample (n_clusters left null for CAHSEE because per-grade classroom counts are not reported). (6) Per-arm student n's for AWA are from Tables 4/5 'All students' rows (Year1 control 851 / Pathway 966; Year2 control 616 / Pathway 634); these baseline-sample n's are slightly larger than the regression N (1817 / 1250) because two Year-1 teachers did not give the AWA posttest. (7) The CST-ELA (California Standards Test) is mentioned only as a baseline covariate/theory-of-change distal outcome and no CST-ELA impact is reported, so no reading-test impact row is extractable.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Pathway Project cognitive-strategies writing PD vs business-as-usual control -- Year 2 (2013-2014, end-of-treatment replication cohort)
effect_sizes.test_name: Academic Writing Assessment (AWA) on-demand text-based analytical essay (scored 2-12)
effect_sizes.g_method: Covariate/pretest-adjusted gain-score regression (Table 6 Model B): Pathway coefficient b=1.30 on the AWA scale, cluster-robust SE=0.20. Standardized by the pooled pretest SD s=1.30/0.60=2.167 (matches paper's reported d). d=b/s=0.6000, se_d=SE/s=0.0923. g=J*d with J=1-3/(4*df-1), df=N-2=1248, J=0.99940, g=0.5996; g_se=J*se_d=0.0923, g_var=g_se^2=0.008510. SEs are Huber-White cluster-robust by classroom -> cluster_adjusted=true.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 6 (Year 2 Model B, p.61); Table 5 means (p.60); results p.35; abstract p.2
effect_sizes.notes: Headline confirmatory writing outcome, Year 2 (paper's end-of-treatment replication; Year-2 students are first-year-program students taught by second-year-program teachers). Reported d=0.60, p<.001. Unadjusted All-students gain difference = 1.22 (Table 5). AWA is a researcher/developer-made on-demand analytical-writing measure most closely tied to the intervention. Writing -> outcome_subject Other. mean/sd are unadjusted Year-2 posttest values (Table 5 All students). Per-arm n from Table 5 baseline (616 control / 634 Pathway); regression N=1250.

effect_sizes.arm_label: Pathway Project cognitive-strategies writing PD vs business-as-usual control -- Year 2 (2013-2014 cohort), 10th-grade subgroup
effect_sizes.test_name: California High School Exit Exam (CAHSEE) -- 10th-grade pass rate (ELA/math state exit exam)
effect_sizes.g_method: Dichotomous pass/fail outcome (Table 8, All 10th grade): control 79/114 passed (69.30%), Pathway 107/122 passed (87.70%), unadjusted difference 18.4 pp (p<.001). g via Cox/logit transform of the odds ratio: OR=(0.877/0.123)/(0.693/0.307)=3.160, d=ln(OR)/1.65=0.6974; Var(d)=Var(lnOR)/1.65^2 with Var(lnOR)=1/107+1/15+1/79+1/35=0.1165, Var(d)=0.04279. g=J*d, df=234, J=0.99678, g=0.6951, g_se=0.2069, g_var=0.04279. NOTE: covariate-adjusted cluster-robust logistic model (Table 9 Model B) gives OR=2.19 (t=0.96, ns) -> d=0.475, g=0.474, g_se=0.493 (non-significant); authors call CAHSEE regression results 'suggestive rather than definitive'. impact_estimate reported here is the unadjusted risk difference (0.184).
effect_sizes.page_ref: Table 8 (p.63, All 10th grade); Table 9 Model B (p.64); results p.37
effect_sizes.notes: CAHSEE = independent state high-school exit exam (standardized_independent); 10th-graders ONLY (a non-randomised grade subset of the 7-12 sample), so is_full_sample=false, grade_band=10. Binary pass-rate outcome -> g is an approximation via the Cox logit transform of the odds ratio, flagged. Unadjusted contrast is large and significant; adjusted logistic model (Table 9) non-significant due to small 10th-grade subsample. Reading/ELA-related literacy exam -> outcome_subject Reading. mean_t/mean_c are pass proportions. pretest_adjusted=false and cluster_adjusted=false because the recorded g is from the UNADJUSTED pass rates; the adjusted-and-clustered version is in g_method/notes.
